title: The Speech That Ended Italian Democracy
topic: Mussolini's January 3, 1925 speech (translated from Italian, with archival photographs)
caption_extra: Translated from Mussolini's January 3, 1925 speech to the Italian Chamber of Deputies (Italian text: Wikisource). Archival photos are public domain via Wikimedia Commons and are from other occasions, not this speech.

beats.narration: January 1925. Opposition deputies have boycotted Italy's parliament since the murder of Giacomo Matteotti.
beats.label: Italian Chamber of Deputies

beats.narration: Mussolini rises and declares: "I alone assume the political, moral, and historical responsibility for everything that has happened."
beats.label: Mussolini speaking, 1932 (different occasion)

beats.narration: He says Italy wants peace, and will get it "with love, if possible, or with force if necessary."
beats.label: Rally crowd, 1926 (different occasion)

beats.narration: Within days, police shut opposition clubs and seized newspapers.
beats.label: Mussolini with officials, 1928

beats.narration: Within two years, Italy was a one-party state.
beats.label: Piazza Venezia crowd, 1940 (different occasion)
